target.title: fix(whatsapp): add listGroupsLive for real-time group directory
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves The WhatsApp channel directory adapter only registered `listGroups` (which reads from the config map `channels.whatsapp.groups`) but did **not** register `listGroupsLive`. The CLI (and other consumers) prefer `listGroupsLive` when available, so users who have active WhatsApp group memberships but an empty config-based groups map would see `No groups found.` from `openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp`. Fixes #76722 ## Why This Change Was Made This PR adds `listWhatsAppDirectoryGroupsLive` that fetches groups from the Baileys socket via `groupFetchAllParticipating()`. The function has two code paths: 1. **Process-local controller** (gateway process): uses the existing `getRegisteredWhatsAppConnectionController()` socket — the fast path when a gateway is running. 2. **Standalone socket** (CLI process): when no process-local controller exists (e.g. `openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp` as a standalone command), opens a temporary Baileys socket using stored auth credentials from disk, fetches group metadata, then closes the socket. Both paths fall back gracefully to the config-backed `listWhatsAppDirectoryGroupsFromConfig` on failure. ## User Impact WhatsApp users who have joined groups but haven't manually configured them in `channels.whatsapp.groups` can now see their real group memberships in the directory — from both the gateway process and the standalone CLI. No config changes required. ## Evidence - `pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/directory-config.test.ts` — 11/11 passed - `pnpm tsgo:test` — passed - Lint + format — passed - Rebased onto `upstream/main` — resolves unrelated CI failures in `check-lint`, `check-test-types` **Real behavior proof** — Linux, Node 24.13.1, commit `0a7ae017e3`, linked WhatsApp account (phone number redacted). Standalone CLI `openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp`: ```console $ openclaw directory groups list --channel whatsapp Groups (4) ┌────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┐ │ ID │ Name │ ├────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┤ │ 120363409866058990@g.us │ openclaw_test │ │ 120363409260302345@g.us │ General │ │ 120363408822325057@g.us │ openclaw_test │ │ 120363408212902124@g.us │ test_group │ └────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┘ ``` 4 groups returned from `groupFetchAllParticipating()`. WhatsApp phone app shows 3 groups — `openclaw_test` (Community), `General`, `test_group`. The API returns 4 entries because `openclaw_test` is a WhatsApp Community which Baileys represents as two separate group JIDs (announcement + sub-group). This is expected protocol-level behavior. > **🖼️ WhatsApp app shows 3 groups: `openclaw_test` (Community), `General`, `test_group` What was not tested: Crabbox cross-platform proof. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
